title: Continuum Backup & Recovery Payment Terms by Tier
content:
Net payment terms, late fees and the non-payment thresholds of a Continuum Backup & Recovery plan follow the plan's tier.

| Tier | Net payment terms (days) | Monthly late fee on an invoice's unpaid balance | Grace period after the due date (calendar days) | Days past due of the oldest unpaid invoice at which new backups are paused | Days in suspension after which the plan may be terminated |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Continuum Backup Basic | 15 | 1.5 percent | 5 | 30 | 30 |
| Continuum Backup Standard | 15 | 1.5 percent | 5 | 30 | 30 |
| Continuum Backup Plus | 30 | 1.5 percent | 5 | 45 | 30 |
| Continuum BDR | 30 | 1.5 percent | 10 | 60 | 45 |
| Continuum DRaaS | 30 | 1.5 percent | 10 | 60 | 45 |
| Continuum DRaaS Premier | 45 | 1.5 percent | 15 | 75 | 60 |

## What each figure measures

- **Net payment terms** — the number of days after an invoice is posted on which it falls due.
- **Monthly late fee** — the monthly late fee, as a percent of an invoice's unpaid balance, charged on an invoice past the grace period. It is 1.5 percent on every tier.
- **Grace period** — the calendar days after the due date before a late fee is assessed.
- **Suspension threshold** — the days past due of the oldest unpaid invoice at which new backups are paused.
- **Termination threshold** — the days in suspension after which the plan may be terminated.

## Comparing tiers (hypothetical invoice)

For a hypothetical invoice posted on day 0 of a calendar count, the figures above place its due date on day 15 on Continuum Backup Basic and Continuum Backup Standard, on day 30 on Continuum Backup Plus, Continuum BDR and Continuum DRaaS, and on day 45 on Continuum DRaaS Premier; its grace period then runs a further 5, 10 or 15 calendar days according to the tier's column above.
